There are new details in the investigation of the mid-air attack aboard a commercial
plane from Dubai to Tel Aviv earlier this week. NPR's Kat Lonsdorf reports the United Arab Emirates
has deemed the incident an attempted terrorist attack. Investigators in the UAE announced that
the Fly Dubai co-pilot who carried out the attack mid-flight assaulted the captain of the plane
using what's called a crash axe, a lightweight emergency tool stored in the cockpit to break
through panels or jam doors in the event of a crash. Investigators said the attacker then
tried to seize control of the plane's flight mechanisms. The plane had 174 people on board,
many of whom are Israeli. Israeli officials had already deemed it an attempted terrorist attack.
Emirati investigators have now agreed. Both the pilot and co-pilot are live and being questioned
and the investigation is ongoing. Israel has said the attacker is from Oman, although that
has yet to be confirmed by Emirati, Saudi, or Omani officials. Kat Lonsdorf, NPR News, Tel Aviv.
The window is closing for registering to vote in the midterm elections in some parts of the country,
NPR's Hansi Lo Wang has a rundown of the upcoming deadlines. This weekend is the last chance for
eligible voters to register or update their registration in Alaska, Rhode Island, and the
U.S. Virgin Islands. In South Carolina, online signups end Sunday, and the state's postmark
deadline for mail-in applications is Monday. Monday is also the voter registration deadline
for American Samoa, Arizona, Indiana, and Ohio, plus many southern states. They include Arkansas,
Florida, Georgia, Kentucky, Mississippi, Tennessee, and Texas. Then, in Missouri,
voter registration for the midterm elections closes on Wednesday. If you're already registered,
you can confirm your status by visiting your state or territory's official election website.
Election officials recommend checking before the deadline, especially if you recently moved,
changed your name, or haven't voted in a while. Hansi Lo Wang, NPR News.
The architect of Tennessee's lethal injection protocols is stepping down from his position
after the second botched execution this year. Marianna Baca Yau reports from member station
WPLN in Nashville. Frank Strada helped design the state's new execution process after a 2020
review found that Tennessee had not properly inspected the drugs it uses to put people to
death. Strada came to Tennessee from Arizona, where he oversaw three botched executions similar
to Wednesday's. Christa Pike did not die after receiving two full doses of pentobarbital. Usually
just one dose is considered lethal. Pike's attorneys say she is unconscious and on a ventilator
at an area hospital following Wednesday's botched execution. For NPR News, I'm Marianna Baca Yau
in Nashville. Cornell University's president says his heart aches for the accuser in the gang rape
case and is promising to improve campus safety. A woman sued Cornell and seven former students
last month, alleging she was drugged and incapacitated while members of a fraternity
assaulted her. You're listening to NPR. RM, the K-pop idol and leader of the globe-trotting boy
band BTS, is now a museum curator and has a new exhibition at the San Francisco Museum of Modern
Art. NPR's Chloe Wildman reports. The exhibition includes well over a hundred works from RM's
collection. It highlights ancient and contemporary Korean paintings, objects and sculptures,
including works by some of RM's favorite artists like Kim Won-ki and Yeon Hyung-kyun. At a press
briefing for the show, the self-deprecating musician said he loves collecting art,
but also feels guilty about it. Do I really need to carry so many unnecessary things that I don't
even need? Have I ended up becoming just a boring rich snore? Well, maybe. RM started collecting
art in 2019. He sings about his passion on tracks like Still Life, Chloe Wildman, NPR News.
The San Francisco Museum of Modern Art is the first to feature the San Frans- the South Korean
superstar's art collection. The average long-term U.S. mortgage rate remained above 7 percent this
week. That's the highest mortgage rate in nearly three years. Mortgage buyer Freddie Mac reports
the benchmark 30-year fixed rate mortgage rose to 7.28 percent. Last week it was 7.03 percent.
A year ago, the average mortgage rate was 6.34 percent. Mortgage rates have now increased for
six weeks in a row. The rate is also the highest since November 22nd of 2023. I'm Lindy Kenyon,
